transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-04-29 15:00 PT | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Tom, Priya (Redwood); Sara, James, Carlos (Acme)

Summary: quick sync on POC quality eval. Tom ran through the recent batch results; there are ~10 prompts with regressions vs baseline. Priya outlined tuning plan and suggested guardrail tweaks. Action items were assigned.

[00:00] Tom Alvarez: okay everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep this to 45, uh, agenda is quality pass on the week - the prompt set, the scoring changes, any regression signals and next steps. Sara you good to start?
[00:12] Sara Kim: yeah thanks Tom, quick context — our BH use-case needs 99% pass on compliance checks and acceptable correctness for financial summarization, we saw a drop in quality on the nightly run, so wanted to walk through which prompts flagged and if it's model drift or prompt issues.
[00:30] Priya Shah: got it. I pulled the spreadsheet, link is in the chat (https://redwood.app/drive/acme-poc/quality-20250429). The baseline was run against rwd-v2-small last week and the new run was rwd-v2-small-quant, there are some tokenization differences and a couple of truncation cases.
[00:45] James Lee: quick clarifying q, when you say "regression" is that strictly on rubric score or also safety flags?
[00:52] Priya Shah: both — mainly rubric score drop for ~10 prompt variants and 3 additional safety/guardrail hits where the filter triggered in the new runs, the rest are within noise.
[01:10] Carlos Mendes: are those guardrail hits false positives? we can't have the filter blocking legitimate client text.
[01:16] Priya Shah: early inspection shows 2 false positives from the new tokenization profile — phrases that include ticker-like strings are being misclassified. We'll tighten the regex and add a sentence-level exception for the summarization route.
[01:30] Tom Alvarez: just to call out, some of this is expected when switching quantized variants; there's a small quality delta sometimes. Our Optimize recommendations suggested a different quant profile but we can iterate.
[01:45] Sara Kim: timeline is tight — we're aiming for pilot by 2025-06-01. We need the false positives eliminated and the top 20 prompt edge cases nailed.
[01:56] Priya Shah: understood. Plan: 1) run targeted regression for the 10 failing prompts with higher precision model variant, 2) adjust guardrails and re-run safety suite, 3) update scoring rubric to clarify pass/fail buckets and threshold. I'll post details to the spreadsheet.
[02:15] Tom Alvarez: can you explain the scoring rubric change? last week the pass threshold was 0.75, right?
[02:23] Priya Shah: yes we used a 0-1 normalized score; suggested tweak is to separate intent/accuracy and format/consistency => two scores per prompt, then an aggregate. That makes regressions easier to triage. Also recommend adding a binary safety flag so any guardrail hit auto-fails regardless of score.
[02:42] Sara Kim: that helps. we need explicit examples in the rubric so our QA can reproduce.
[02:48] Priya Shah: will add examples and edge-case notes.
[02:55] James Lee: ops question — how are we logging these runs? is there a per-token breakdown in the console we can share with infra?
[03:03] Tom Alvarez: yes the Redwood Console shows per-route token counts, latency percentiles and cost. We'll export the traces for the failing prompts; there's also a benchmark CSV in the drive.
[03:15] James Lee: perfect. also we've been tracking latency spikes in our staging cluster, any relation to these regressions?
[03:21] Priya Shah: unlikely — the regressions seem quality-focused not latency. but we will correlate the timestamps to rule it out. Could be that truncation due to KV cache mismatch caused shorter contexts, that's on the infra side to check.
[03:40] Carlos Mendes: can you remind me of the fallback policy? if the quantized worker has worse output we want automatic fallback to the higher-fidelity model, right?
[03:48] Tom Alvarez: yes — we support model variant routing and automated fallback. For the POC we can enable a policy: if scoring drops below N prompts threshold in a 10-min window, route to high-fidelity variant for that user cohort. We can also do canary rollouts.
[04:02] Sara Kim: is enabling fallback going to increase cost dramatically? we have budget constraints.
[04:09] Priya Shah: it will increase token cost but only for the cohort affected; optimize config can limit duration and scope. We can model the cost impact in the spreadsheet.
[04:20] Tom Alvarez: action: I'll add a cost delta column to the benchmark sheet so you can see worst-case.
[04:26] Sara Kim: thanks.
[04:30] Priya Shah: jumping back to the 10 failing prompts — two categories: format regressions (bad bullet formatting, missing headers) and semantic regressions (incorrect amounts or mis-stated risk language). Format is easy to fix with stricter output schema and a post-processing guardrail. Semantic requires nudging prompts or using higher-temp constraints.
[04:52] James Lee: Can we just post-process formatting always? would that hide underlying quality issues?
[04:57] Priya Shah: you can but we recommend validating first; post-process helps UX but doesn't fix incorrect facts. We'll add both: post-process for formatting + scoring checks for semantic correctness.
[05:12] Tom Alvarez: also consider function-calling or structured output enforcement, that reduces hallucinations for fields like amounts.
[05:20] Sara Kim: we tried structured output in week 1, it helped but had edge cases in nested lists, maybe we should iterate that approach.
[05:28] Priya Shah: agreed — we'll create a small A/B: structured output vs free text with post-process for the 20 problematic prompts.
[05:38] Carlos Mendes: when you say "A/B" how will we split and measure?
[05:42] Priya Shah: split by prompt id and user cohort; measure on the rubric and safety flags, plus latency and cost delta. We'll show side-by-side in the spreadsheet.
[05:52] Tom Alvarez: can you call out the 10 prompts now? just list IDs so we all have the same reference.
[05:58] Priya Shah: sure — IDs in the sheet: P-112, P-115, P-118, P-129, P-133, P-137, P-141, P-149, P-152, P-158. I'll paste them in chat.
[06:10] Sara Kim: thanks. we also flagged a couple of prompts that are flaky with SSO tokens in the input, that might be a masking/parsing issue.
[06:18] Priya Shah: noted — we'll sanitize that in the preprocessor.
[06:22] James Lee: on the compliance front, we need audit logs for all inference requests and also key rotation details. Are those available in Private deployments?
[06:32] Tom Alvarez: yes Private and Dedicated both support KMS integration and audit logging. For hosted we have an audit log export and SOC2 evidence; details in the security pack. I'll attach the security doc (link in chat).
[06:45] Sara Kim: please send over the exact retention options and PII redaction defaults.
[06:50] Tom Alvarez: will do — action for me.
[06:53] Priya Shah: returning to scoring — the current pass threshold of 0.75 produced false negatives in a few cases; suggest adding a "review" bucket for 0.65-0.75 where QA does a manual check before failing. That reduces noisy re-runs.
[07:06] Carlos Mendes: I like the review bucket. we can budget for a small manual check during pilot.
[07:12] Sara Kim: ok. any update on the three safety hits — are they reproducible?
[07:18] Priya Shah: two are reproducible with the quant variant, one is intermittent. We'll run a 500-sample safety harness and report hit rate.
[07:28] Tom Alvarez: please include the example inputs/outputs for each hit in the report.
[07:33] Priya Shah: will do.
[07:36] James Lee: minor infra note — we saw occasional tokenization mismatch when the client truncates before the end-of-prompt, that yields different context length. We should align preproc logic.
[07:47] Priya Shah: yep preprocessor fix is low-effort. we'll push that change to staging and re-run.
[07:54] Tom Alvarez: timeline recapped: Priya does regression and guardrail fixes by 2025-05-05, Tom shares updated prompt-set and rubric by 2025-05-02, Sara sends compliance list by 2025-05-01. If regressions remain we schedule perf/technical deep dive week of 2025-05-06.
[08:10] Sara Kim: that works. also, can you include notes on fallback policy and cost deltas in the next update?
[08:18] Tom Alvarez: yep I will.
[08:20] Carlos Mendes: anything else on the scoring granularity?
[08:24] Priya Shah: just one more: we'll add categorical tags to prompts (format, semantic, safety) to make triage faster.
[08:31] Tom Alvarez: great. last thing — I'll share a short video walkthrough of how to interpret the spreadsheet for non-engineers.
[08:38] Sara Kim: appreciated.
[08:40] Tom Alvarez: ok thanks all, we'll reconvene same time next week unless the deep dive is needed earlier.
[08:46] Meeting end.

Notes/References: benchmark spreadsheet: https://redwood.app/drive/acme-poc/quality-20250429 | security pack: https://redwood.app/security/acme-pack | example failing outputs pasted in spreadsheet under tab "regressions".

Transcript quality notes: auto transcription had speaker swaps and occasional mis-hear of technical terms (e.g., "KV cache" transcribed as "K V cache").

Recap of next steps: Tom to send rubric + cost deltas; Priya to run regressions and post results; Sara to send compliance list.
